newsitem.title: USA: US consumer confidence jumps-Conference Bd.
newsitem.headline: US consumer confidence jumps-Conference Bd.

text.p: The index of U.S. consumer confidence jumped to 113.8 in December, up from a revised reading of 109.5 in November, the Conference Board said Tuesday.

"Consumer confidence is up dramatically over the last 12 months, suggesting that consumer demand will help pave the way for a healthy economy during the first half of 1997," Lynn Franco, associate director of the private research group's Consumer Research Centre, said in a statement.
The consumer confidence report said "consumers are more positive now than they were in November, with nearly 29 percent saying that jobs are plentiful, up from less than 27 percent in November."
Less than 6 percent of surveyed households said they were looking for a slowdown in economic activity, the report said.
